title: Combat
markdown:
# Combat

Combat in D&D is played in **rounds** of about 6 seconds of in-game time. Each round every creature involved takes a **turn** in initiative order.

## The Order of Combat

1. **Roll initiative.** Everyone involved in combat rolls 1d20 + Dexterity modifier. The DM sorts combatants from highest to lowest.
2. **Take turns.** On your turn you can **Move** up to your speed and take **one Action**. You may also take **one Bonus Action** and any number of **Reactions** before your next turn.
3. **End of turn.** Effects that trigger "at the end of your turn" happen now. After everyone has taken a turn, the round ends and a new one begins.

## Actions in Combat

When you take your Action you can choose from several options (see the full list in the *Player's Handbook / SRD 5.2*):

- **Attack** — make one melee or ranged attack (or more with features like *Extra Attack*).
- **Cast a Spell** — if you have a spell prepared and an available slot.
- **Dash**, **Disengage**, **Dodge** — move faster, avoid opportunity attacks, or impose disadvantage on incoming attacks.
- **Help** — give an ally advantage on their next check or attack.
- **Hide**, **Search**, **Study** — Stealth, Perception, or Investigation checks.
- **Ready** — prepare an action with a trigger to use later as a reaction.
- **Use an Object** or **grapple / shove** a creature.

## Movement and Opportunity Attacks

You can break up your movement however you like during your turn. If you leave a hostile creature's reach, that creature can make **one opportunity attack** against you — unless you **Disengage**, you have the *Sentinel* feat, or you teleport instead of using movement.

## Cover

Targets can benefit from cover, making them harder to hit:

- **Half cover** — +2 bonus to AC and Dexterity saving throws.
- **Three-quarters cover** — +5 bonus.
- **Total cover** — can't be targeted directly.

## Hit Points and Damage

When you take damage, subtract it from your current hit points. When you drop to **0 hit points**, you're unconscious and dying (death saving throws) — or killed instantly by certain effects. Healing of any kind restores hit points, up to your maximum.

## Death Saving Throws

When you're at 0 HP and not killed outright, you roll a death save at the start of each of your turns. Roll 10 or higher to succeed; roll 9 or lower to fail. Three successes stabilize you. Three failures kill you. A **20** counts as two successes; a **1** counts as two failures.

## Conditions

Creatures can be affected by conditions such as *blinded*, *grappled*, *paralyzed*, *poisoned*, *prone*, *restrained*, *stunned*, *unconscious*, and others. Each condition imposes specific benefits and limitations — refer to the **Conditions** table for full details.
